check: correct a reporting error of mine: I had been printing a hardcoded refill count
whatWentWrong: Every status line I printed for many rounds ended with 'refills=13'. That was a literal string in my command, not a read value. It was correct when first written and stayed in the template afterwards.

theTrueValue.verdict: The profile has refilled 36 times, not 13.

whyItMatters: Refills are the profile's liveness signal - the earlier work established that a run which stops refilling has quietly drained its queue and will end early. Reporting a stale count as if current is exactly the failure that signal exists to detect, and it would have hidden a healthy pattern behind a frozen number.
whatIsStillTrue: The health judgement was never wrong, only the number. ERROR 0, watchdog 0 and OutOfMemory 0 are all read values, and threads remain flat at 33 across five hours and 36 refills.
theFix: The status command now reads every figure from the log and the latest sample rather than carrying any of them as text. Nothing in the printed line is a constant.
methodNote: This is the second error of this kind in the session, after the hardcoded HEAD in the report. Both came from writing a value once and reusing the surrounding text afterwards. The habit worth keeping is that a status line should contain no literals at all.
